output.summary: Recover and approve the brainstorm decisions that decision-row type selects the pipeline, loop quality profile, and evidence policy.

approvedRows.question: Should decision rows own selection of the pipeline profile used by downstream loops?
approvedRows.currentState: Decision rows currently classify decisionKind, workScale, planningDepth, routeTarget, and direct implementation scope, while loop graphs run their default full node sets. The brainstorm agreed that those row fields are not enough to express different safe lanes such as debug, fix, harden, migrate, docs, release, and direct implementation.
approvedRows.desiredState: Each approved decision row carries or resolves to a decision type. That decision type selects a pipelineProfile, which determines route target, planning depth, direct implementation eligibility, escalation behavior, and downstream loop activation expectations.
approvedRows.rationale: The pipeline must be trace-backed and row-owned so routing and quality expectations are explainable, reproducible, and not silently chosen by runtime heuristics.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get the right amount of process for the type of work: smaller safe changes can move faster, while risky work escalates before false passes occur.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must add a typed registry and keep routing decisions test-backed rather than embedding ad hoc route logic in each loop.
approvedRows.routeRationale: This is a foundational system behavior change that needs planned slices before implementation.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: This matches the brainstorm and current refactor goal while preserving the three-loop architecture.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: User asked to recover the brainstorm decisions before starting the refactor.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Makes pipeline routing explicit, trace-backed, and testable.
agentAssessment.rationale: Current rows already carry partial routing fields; a profile registry is the simpler extension point.

approvedRows.currentPain: Pipeline behavior is distributed across row fields and loop defaults, so the reason a row takes a route or quality profile is not represented as a first-class policy object.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Decision row type resolves to a named pipeline profile with deterministic route and loop-quality profile selection.
approvedRows.successSignal: Tests can assert decision type to pipeline profile mapping and fail closed for unknown or disallowed combinations.
nonGoals: Do not add a fourth semantic loop.
Do not let runtime own semantic route authority.
Do not remove existing decisionKind, workScale, planningDepth, or routeTarget validation without compatibility handling.

approvedRows.question: Should loop quality profiles activate subsets of the quality network instead of deleting or mutating graph nodes?
approvedRows.currentState: Loop quality graphs are frozen production networks with node definitions, graph versions, hashes, gates, costs, and judge specs. The brainstorm concluded that decision-specific quality should not mutate those production graphs in user projects.
approvedRows.desiredState: A loopQualityProfile is an activation mask over the frozen production quality network. Nodes can be active, required, optional, escalated, or explicitly not applicable, but node definitions remain stable and graph identity remains explainable.
approvedRows.rationale: Activation masks allow decision-type-specific process while preserving graph hashes, lab-trained behavior, auditability, and false-pass resistance.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get less irrelevant process noise without weakening required safety checks for their work type.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must represent inactive node reasons and test that hard safety gates cannot disappear silently.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Needs data model, evaluation behavior, docs, and regression tests.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: This preserves frozen network integrity while allowing profile-specific quality selection.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches the brainstorm note that quality profile subsets are activation masks, not deletion.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Maintains stable quality graph identities and improves right-reason scoring.
agentAssessment.rationale: Failing closed on missing activation reasons is safer than mutating graphs.

approvedRows.currentPain: All loop executions currently expose the same quality graph shape without a first-class profile reason for node activation or non-applicability.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Loop outputs record profile activation state and reasons such as not_applicable, covered_by_invariant, or escalated_elsewhere for inactive nodes.
approvedRows.successSignal: Tests prove profile masks preserve graph identity, require reasons for inactive nodes, and fail closed when required nodes are skipped without allowed reason.
nonGoals: Do not train or mutate production quality networks live in user projects.
Do not treat an inactive node as passed.
Do not hide skipped hard gates without a profile-authorized reason.

approvedRows.question: Should decision type select evidence policy while CodeWiki retains semantic authority over external tools?
approvedRows.currentState: Implementation review has CodeWiki-owned evidence reports and path-language review pack dispatch, but evidence expectations are not yet tied to decision-row type. Fast cached evidence can block but does not satisfy acceptance coverage.
approvedRows.desiredState: Each decision type definition includes evidencePolicy. The policy declares required evidence classes, review pack requirements, acceptance-link expectations, fast-cache reuse limits, and escalation triggers. External tools remain sensors; CodeWiki quality standards decide pass/fail.
approvedRows.rationale: Different work types need different proof without making lint, typecheck, or judge scores authoritative by themselves.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get stronger proof for risky work and faster feedback for low-risk work without accepting false passes from clean tool output alone.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must keep evidence policy normalized, language-portable, and independent from Pi-lens, Pi-posher, Caveman, or any host extension.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Evidence policy touches implementation review and config behavior, so it needs planned slices.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: This codifies existing review architecture decisions and connects them to decision-row types.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches the brainstorm decision that decisionType maps to evidencePolicy and that tools are evidence only.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Improves false-pass resistance and right-reason scoring across implementation review.
agentAssessment.rationale: A policy object is clearer and safer than inferring proof needs from file extensions alone.

approvedRows.currentPain: Review packs auto-dispatch by path, but decision intent does not yet declare which evidence classes are mandatory, optional, or escalation-only.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Evidence policy is selected from decision type and merged with project config without giving external tools semantic authority.
approvedRows.successSignal: Tests can assert required evidence for fix, harden, migrate, docs, release, and direct implementation profiles, including fail-closed behavior when required evidence is missing.
nonGoals: Do not require per-language project config by default.
Do not make lint clean equivalent to implementation correct.
Do not allow fast-only cached evidence to satisfy acceptance coverage.

approvedRows.question: Should decision type definitions include escalation rules and forbidden skips?
approvedRows.currentState: Current route rules reject many unsafe direct implementation cases, but the rules are spread across loop validation and are not represented as reusable type policy. The brainstorm identified false pass as the highest-cost error.
approvedRows.desiredState: Each DecisionTypeDefinition includes escalationRules and forbiddenSkips. Escalation rules route rows to planning, user approval, stronger evidence, or earlier-loop repair when risk, ambiguity, scope, security, release, dependency, or multi-component signals appear. Forbidden skips prevent profiles from disabling critical hard gates, trace coverage, acceptance evidence, content proof, or required review evidence.
approvedRows.rationale: Making escalation and forbidden skips explicit prevents process profiles from becoming a loophole around safety gates.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users can trust faster lanes because unsafe work is forced back into stronger process before implementation exit.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must test fail-closed behavior for unknown types, conflicting profile fields, and attempts to skip protected standards.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Hardening policy needs schema, tests, and loop integration planning.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: False-pass resistance requires profile policy to fail closed, not merely recommend stronger process.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches the brainstorm decision that false pass is highest-cost and forbidden skips are required.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Protects hard gates while still allowing decision-type-specific profiles.
agentAssessment.rationale: Escalation policy is simpler to audit when colocated with the decision type definition.

approvedRows.currentPain: Unsafe skips are prevented in scattered checks, but there is no profile-owned declaration of which skips are impossible for a decision type.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Decision type policy fails closed for unknown types, missing profiles, disallowed direct implementation, and attempts to skip protected quality standards.
approvedRows.successSignal: Negative tests prove unknown decision types, forbidden skip attempts, and unsafe direct implementation profiles block before downstream execution.
nonGoals: Do not make escalation a fourth loop.
Do not let runtime override semantic loop authority.
Do not allow profile config to weaken user approval or traceability requirements.

approvedRows.question: Should CodeWiki introduce a first-class DecisionTypeDefinition registry as the implementation seam?
approvedRows.currentState: Decision type is currently represented mostly by decisionKind plus routing fields, not by a registry that maps to pipeline, quality, evidence, escalation, and forbidden-skip policy.
approvedRows.desiredState: Introduce a DecisionTypeDefinition registry with at least id, description, routing, pipelineProfile, loopQualityProfile, evidencePolicy, escalationRules, and forbiddenSkips. Built-in definitions are deterministic, package-owned, and covered by tests; project config may add policy only through guarded extension points that cannot weaken built-in hard gates.
approvedRows.rationale: A registry gives the refactor a narrow implementation seam and makes future decision types auditable and testable.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get consistent behavior across sessions and can understand why a row used a given lane.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers must version and test the registry and keep package defaults frozen unless changed by trace-backed implementation.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Registry and integration need executable work units before implementation.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: This is the smallest safe seam for implementing the recovered design.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches the requested refactor and the brainstorm registry field list.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Keeps type-driven behavior explicit and extensible without ad hoc branches.
agentAssessment.rationale: A typed registry can be introduced before behavior rewiring, reducing risk.

approvedRows.currentPain: There is no single package-owned place to answer what a debug, fix, harden, improve, migrate, docs, release, or direct implementation row means for downstream pipeline and quality.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: The first implementation slice adds registry types/defaults/tests without behavior rewiring, then later slices wire route, profile, and evidence policy consumption.
approvedRows.successSignal: Type and unit tests prove the registry contains built-in decision types, stable ids, safe defaults, and fail-closed lookup behavior.
nonGoals: Do not implement every downstream behavior in the first slice.
Do not expose live mutation of production profiles in user projects.
Do not depend on Pi extensions for registry behavior.

implementationAssessment.maintainability: Decision type definitions isolate policy data while loop/profile/review integrations use small shared helpers and tests.
implementationAssessment.simplicity: No fourth loop or runtime semantic branch added; existing Decision, Planning, and Implementation surfaces receive profile/evidence constraints.
implementationAssessment.projectStyle: Matches existing fail-closed loop standards, trace refs, view summaries, and review-pack policy patterns.
implementationAssessment.errorHandling: Unknown decision types, invalid profile masks, forbidden skips, unsafe direct routes, missing evidence links, and weakening overrides fail closed with diagnostics.
implementationAssessment.rationale: All planned work units have code/docs/tests plus targeted and full-suite verification evidence.

sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.security: Security-sensitive hardening is policy-only and escalates unsafe release/security/dependency rows instead of weakening gates.
sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.accessibility: No interactive UI behavior changed by decision-type policy.
sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.dependencyRisk: No dependencies changed; required review packs remain config/policy data.
sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.rationale: Changes affect workflow policy, quality profiles, and review evidence semantics.

qualityStandards.description: Every planned work ref is covered by implementation evidence and no unknown planning refs are introduced.
Implementation changes stay inside planned component/path scope and existing repo paths.
Every planned acceptance criterion is covered by structured evidence refs.
Required implementation checks are structured, present, passing, cover planned verification, and package changes include pack verification.
Required red/green TDD evidence is mapped to planned acceptance criteria.
Implementation output has change-level and aggregate content proof when required.
Worker-produced evidence is tied to active runtime claims and completed worker results.
Changed source/test paths align with source-map component ownership and test coverage.
Agent assessment records maintainability, simplicity, project style, and error-handling readiness.
CodeWiki-owned review evidence has no blocking diagnostics and links acceptance criteria to concrete evidence.
Independent judge verifies implementation evidence actually supports the claimed changes and acceptance criteria.
Independent judge verifies passing checks are relevant to changed behavior rather than generic or unrelated proof.
Independent judge verifies the production-readiness assessment is specific and not hand-wavy.
No unresolved implementation uncertainty remains; planning, decision, or user authority is routed instead of drifting.
Security/privacy-sensitive changes include explicit review evidence.
UI/page changes include accessibility review evidence.
Dependency-surface changes include risk review evidence.
Release, publication, destructive, or externally visible implementation refs require explicit user approval.
Implementation refs are canonical trace, KB, Git, digest, source, or test refs.
